x: Foord of Brighton and Barrett, SAC. were first and second almost from the start and never looked as though they would be replaced. When the field had settled down, Jim Masters was running 3rd with Baker of the local club who eventually beat him and our scoring six were in the first thirty.

Pirie, Norris and Foord fought it out all the way and our chaps were never in the hunt for the leading positions. Our leading runner just managed to beat South London's 6th, but by some remarkable packing, six men in 14 places and 64 seconds, we gained second place in the team race.
He held his position by steady running, until half-way up the aerodrome stretch of Purley Way when Foord of Brighton, running in fine style, sailed past.

The large field set off at a terrific pace and among the first 6 were soon seen Foord (Brighton), who won for the fourth time, Ernie Earl (Hercules), Tony Weckes-Pearson (Blackheath) and our own Charlie Dabbs.
Pirie was an easy winner for S.L.H. smashing previous course records set by Hyman and Foord by nearly a minute. Ken Miller was a good third, with Thresher 7th, Walker 8th and Shippen 10th.

This is the leg where the race can be won and lost, and names such as Hyman (who produced a fantastic new record - 34 seconds better than his own previous best), Wilkinson, Perry, North, Reed, Edmonds, Hogan and Foord appeared - enough to frighten the stoutest of hearts.
